description: Fixed-point arithmetic primitives modelled on top of std/core.mm and std/math/safe_mul.mm. Conversions between integer and fixed-point representation, plus overflow-safe add and rescaling multiplication. Proven with Z3 integer theory only — no real arithmetic required. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/math/fixed_point — verified fixed-point arithmetic'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/math/safe_mul.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT invent new operators, types, or syntax — use only what std/core.mm and std/math/safe_mul.mm already use (checked_add, checked_mul, safe_mul, conditional expressions).

atoms.name: fixed_from_int
atoms.description: Convert a non-negative integer to fixed-point representation by multiplying by `scale`. The scale is bounded so the product fits comfortably within i64.

atoms.name: fixed_to_int
atoms.description: Convert a fixed-point value back to an integer by dividing by `scale`. The contract proves the truncated result is non-negative and that result * scale never exceeds the original fixed value (i.e. truncation is monotone non-increasing).

atoms.name: fixed_add
atoms.description: Overflow-safe fixed-point addition. The caller supplies `max_val` as an upper bound that the result must respect.

atoms.name: fixed_mul
atoms.description: Fixed-point multiplication with rescaling. The product is divided by `scale` to keep the result in fixed-point representation, and clamped at `max_val`.
